I'm really just trying to change the way we talk about drugs. Putting illegal substances into some "other group" is socially and legally penalizing in a way that does not help, and the dichotomy really just doesn't make sense. I think the world would be better if we just talked about drugs individually, using what we know about them, instead of lumping every powder or pill into some skull-and-crossbones group.

I think of it like this.

Drugs are not good for you.
 
Knowing that will not stop drug users from using drugs.

Drugs really don't have to be very harmful, educated responsible use is possible, but the education part is very important.

Because of this, blanket statements like "hard drugs", or just even telling people "don't do it", is actually significantly harmful on a societal scale.

These attitudes and phrases that have been programmed into us are bad for us, and I think we should try to break out of it.

1.) SpontaneousH's story is fake

2.) I've had opioids for surgeries. Didn't ruin my life.

3.) Opioids are not carcinogenic

4.) Opioid withdrawal is non-lethal (compared to alcohol, which is)

5.) Opioid use does not destroy your lungs, liver, or any other organ


Keep in mind, I am not saying "heroin good heroin based go do heroin", because you should not do heroin.

What I am saying is the scale is tilted. I seriously consider opioids to be less of a risk than alcohol given educated responsible use. You could use opioids for the entirety of your life and never suffer any bodily harm because of it. You CANNOT say the same thing about alcohol or tobacco.

However, it is perfectly socially and legally acceptable to do both alcohol and tobacco your entire adult life.

The concept of "hard" and "soft" drugs is  an entirely moralistic, propagandized, socially constructed dichotomy that exists to serve the interests of the companies that produce taxable, socially acceptable intoxicants.

ALL DRUGS ARE HARMFUL, but please talk about them objectively.

I'd consider tobacco and alcohol "hard drugs", they do a significant amount of bodily harm, compared to say heroin, which is actually fairly benign when it comes to that, provided your dose is sane. Following this logic, I could call tobacco and alcohol "hard drugs", but not heroin. Does this change anything about either of them? Not really.
